statement: For the frozen K_5 problem at p=1/2, let F(r), 3/4 <= r <= 1, be the minimum unconditional success probability over every admissible jointly defined family of auxiliary events with each event probability at least r. Then F(r) equals (182/207)r on [3/4,207/256], (19/18)r-73/512 on [207/256,243/256], (4/3)r-13/32 on [243/256,63/64], and 2r-17/16 on [63/64,1]. In particular, for r=1-t^2 and every 0<t<=1/2, F(1-t^2)>(15/16)(1-2t), so the frozen inequality holds for the complete p=1/2 slice.
contribution: An exact four-branch classification of the worst admissible joint auxiliary-event kernel on a nonplanar K_5 parameter slice. It upgrades the previous single-point LP calculation to every epsilon in the frozen range and proves a substantive subsidiary case while leaving all p != 1/2 cases unresolved. The bounded primary-source screen found no equivalent K_5 classification, but no priority or formal open-status claim is made.
